arxiv-1407-1640.title: WordRep: A Benchmark for Research on Learning Word Representations
arxiv-1407-1640.creator: Bin Gao, Jiang Bian, Tie-Yan Liu
arxiv-1407-1640.description: Abstract WordRep is a benchmark collection for the research on learning distributed word representations (or word embeddings), released by Microsoft Research. In this paper, we describe the details of the WordRep collection and show how to use it in different types of machine learning research related to word embedding.

arxiv-2211-15230.title: Stability of Minkowski spacetime in exterior regions
arxiv-2211-15230.creator: Dawei Shen
arxiv-2211-15230.description: Abstract In 1993, the global stability of Minkowski spacetime has been proven in the celebrated work of Christodoulou and Klainerman [ 5 ] in a maximal foliation. In 2003, Klainerman and Nicolò [ 14 ] gave a second proof of the stability of Minkowski in the case of the exterior of an outgoing null cone.

arxiv-2406-09215.title: On Softmax Direct Preference Optimization for Recommendation
arxiv-2406-09215.creator: Yuxin Chen Junfei Tan An Zhang, Zhengyi Yang Leheng Sheng Enzhi Zhang, Xiang Wang Tat-Seng Chua
arxiv-2406-09215.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yuxin Chen Junfei Tan An Zhang, Zhengyi Yang Leheng Sheng Enzhi Zhang, Xiang Wang Tat-Seng Chua. Recommender systems aim to predict personalized rankings based on user preference data. With the rise of Language Models (LMs), LM-based recommenders have been widely explored due to their extensive world knowledge and powerful reasoning abilities. Most of the LM-based recommenders convert historical interactions into language prompts, pairing with a positive item as the target response and fine-tuning LM with a language modeling loss.

arxiv-2509-11704.creator: Chieh Tsao
arxiv-2509-11704.description: Abstract Abstract Harnessing quantum correlations between photons is an emerging direction in optical spectroscopy, but experimental progress has thus far been limited to fluorescence-detected studies of molecular systems at room temperature. Here, we demonstrate heralded emission detection (HED) under continuous-wave (CW) entangled-photon excitation of near-infrared (NIR)–emitting colloidal III–V quantum dots (QDs) at low temperatures.

pmc-11434641.title: Adherence to Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) Diet as a Protective Factor for Ischemic Stroke and Its Influence on Disability Level: A Case–Control Study in Lebanon
pmc-11434641.creator: Jad El Masri, Hani Finge, Tarek Baroud, Najla Ajaj, Mariam Houmani, Maya Ghazi, Mahmoud Younes, Pascale Salameh, Hassan Hosseini
pmc-11434641.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Hypertension is a major risk factor for ischemic stroke. An important strategy in controlling hypertension is dietary modification. The present study evaluates the effect of Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet on the risk of ischemic stroke. Methods: A case–control study was carried out, including 214 ischemic stroke cases recruited within the first 48 h of diagnosis and 214 controls, divided equally into hospitalized and non-hospitalized participants. Controls were matched to cases based on age and gender.

pmc-11728403.title: A Comparative Study of the Electroneurographic Findings in Amyloidotic Polyneuropathy in Patients with Light-Chain Amyloidosis and Glu54Gln Transthyretin Amyloidosis
pmc-11728403.creator: Mirela Drăghici, Sorina N Bădeliță, Andreea Jercan, Oana Obrișcă, Crisanda Vîlciu, Monica Popescu, Adina Turcu-Stiolica, Daniel Coriu, Jung-Ho Lee
pmc-11728403.description: Background and Objectives: Amyloidosis is a disorder characterized by the abnormal folding of proteins, forming insoluble fibrils that accumulate in tissues and organs. This accumulation disrupts normal tissue architecture and organ function, often with serious consequences, including death if left untreated. Light-chain amyloidosis (AL) and hereditary transthyretin-type amyloidosis (hATTR) are two of the most common types.

pmc-12655573.title: Joint Bacterial Traces in the Gut and Oral Cavity of Obesity Patients Provide Evidence for Saliva as a Rich Microbial Biomarker Source
pmc-12655573.creator: Jacqueline Rehner, Madline Gund, Sören L. Becker, Matthias Hannig, Stefan Rupf, Jörn M. Schattenberg, Andreas Keller, the IMAGINE Consortium, Leidy-Alejandra G. Molano, Verena Keller
pmc-12655573.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: The human microbiome holds promise for identifying biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In obesity, interactions between oral and gut communities are increasingly implicated and end in organ injury. Methods: From the IMAGINE study, we analyzed 418 shotgun metagenomes from three specimen types (dental plaque (n = 143; 65 non-obese, 78 obese), saliva (n = 166; 75 non-obese, 91 obese), and stool (n = 109; 57 non-obese, 52 obese)) to compare site-specific microbial shifts between obese (BMI > 30 kg/m2) and non-obese individuals.

pmc-13578451.title: Focal mechanism variations reveal mechanical controls on segmentation at oceanic transform faults
pmc-13578451.creator: Fengzhou Tan, Wenyuan Fan, Peter M Shearer, Mark D Behn, Jeffrey J McGuire
pmc-13578451.description: Oceanic transform faults (OTFs) exhibit concurrent slip behaviors, with creep and characteristic earthquakes on localized patches. At the Gofar transform fault on the East Pacific Rise, magnitude 5.5+ earthquakes are bounded by creeping segments that act as persistent rupture barriers, yet the physical controls on this segmentation remain unclear.
